paragraphs: Here's what hit me, friend. An Amalekite comes to David with Saul's crown and armband and says he killed Saul (2 Samuel 1:10). But David doesn't celebrate. He tears his clothes, and he mourns and weeps and fasts until evening for Saul and Jonathan, and for the people of the LORD (2 Samuel 1:11-12).

Now think about who Saul was to David. This is the same king who searched for David every day (1 Samuel 23:14), and David still sang, "Saul and Jonathan, beloved and delightful in life, were not divided in death" (2 Samuel 1:23). David also asked the Amalekite, "Why were you not afraid to lift your hand to destroy the LORD's anointed?" (2 Samuel 1:14). So David wasn't just sad. He took the LORD's anointed seriously, even when that anointed king was the one who had been chasing him.

So here's the lesson for you, baker. Grief and honor can sit in the same heart as hard history, and you don't have to cheer when someone who hurt you falls. David could have grabbed that crown and run. Instead he cried, and he sang "How the mighty have fallen!" (2 Samuel 1:19). Let that rub off on you, and be the kind of person who mourns what's lost, even when a lot of people would say you've got every reason to clap.
